clue.text: Second fall, or nearly so

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for second, as in units of time
to tumble is to take a fall

explanation.surface: A wrestler goes down a second time, or almost does.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a stumble is a second-rate fall, one that nearly happens but not quite.
explanation.definitionFit: A stumble is a trip that almost becomes a tumble, a lesser kind of falling over.

clue.text: Rose to be an author and stay after time

indicators.note: after says the word for stay follows the letter for time

parts.note: to remain is to stay

explanation.surface: A flower becomes a writer and lingers once time is up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rose' is not a flower or a verb but the first name of the novelist Rose Tremain.
explanation.definitionFit: Rose Tremain is a British novelist, so with Rose in front the surname names a writer.

clue.text: Big beast sounds little in Scotland

indicators.note: sounds says we hear the word spoken rather than spelt
in Scotland points to the Scots pronunciation of the word

parts.note: a mouse is a proverbially little creature, Burns's wee beastie

explanation.surface: A huge animal's call turns out to be tiny north of the border.
explanation.walkthrough: In Scots a mouse is pronounced 'moose'.
explanation.definitionFit: The moose is the largest deer, a very big animal of northern forests.

clue.text: Most of 12 with Danish king for security

indicators.note: most of means the word is cut short, losing its tail

parts.note: 12 is a town tavern, a pub, which is a local
Knut (Canute) was a Danish king of England

explanation.surface: Much of a pub is handed to a Danish king to keep it safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 12 is TAVERN IN THE TOWN; a pub is a LOCAL, and losing AL leaves LOC.
explanation.definitionFit: A locknut is a second nut screwed down to secure the first, a device used for security.

clue.text: Demo at expert game in 9, say

parts.note: a pro is a professional, an expert
a Test is an international match, such as one in the Rugby World Cup (9-down)

explanation.surface: A demonstration staged at a top-level match during a big tournament.
explanation.definitionFit: A demo is short for a demonstration, a public show of objection.

clue.text: Niche for holiday?

definitions.meaning: an alcove set back in a wall
a break from parliament or school

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a hollow in a wall and a period when business is suspended.

clue.text: Good guy in 9 has youth clubs quivering with terror

indicators.note: quivering suggests the letters shaking and rearranging

parts.note: 's is a short form of has, as in it's been
C stands for clubs, the card suit
taken as written

explanation.surface: A youngster joins clubs and trembles with fear.
explanation.definitionFit: In a rugby tournament the player who touches the ball down for a try is the hero of the moment.

clue.text: Part of 9 setter's is delicious

parts.note: a scrum is part of a rugby match (9-down)
the setter refers to themself, so setter's is my

explanation.surface: A slice of the tournament, says the compiler, tastes wonderful.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrummy is informal British for scrumptious, tasty.

clue.text: Warmer student in perfect example caught up in recent event

parts.note: a rug keeps you warm

indicators.note: in says the student's letter goes inside the word for perfect example

parts.note: a byword is a perfect example of something
L is a learner, a student driver
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
taken as written

explanation.surface: A heater and a student are caught up in something that has just happened.
explanation.walkthrough: The 2011 tournament in New Zealand had just finished when the puzzle appeared.
explanation.definitionFit: The tournament had just taken place, so it was a recent happening.

clue.text: See 27
See 21
Teacher's first to state last of 9 was leader in school, not 21 pub

indicators.note: first signals that only the opening letter of the word teacher's is used

parts.note: to aver is to state firmly
the last of nine things in a row is the ninth

indicators.note: in says the letter from was goes inside the name of the school

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the word was is taken

explanation.surface: A teacher's tale of a former head boy, set in a city pub rather than a rural one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Teacher's first' gives T; W (the leader of 'was') goes inside ETON. 'not 21' means not COUNTRY, so the pub is in the town; 'There is a Tavern in the Town' is an old drinking song.
explanation.definitionFit: A town tavern is an urban pub, the opposite of a country one; the phrase is also a well-known song title.

clue.text: HQ for expedition to find Cambridgeshire ape

indicators.note: to find here hints that the letters must be sorted out and rearranged to discover a new word

parts.note: Cambs is the standard short form of the English county Cambridgeshire
taken as written

explanation.surface: Explorers set up headquarters to track down an ape loose in Cambridgeshire.
explanation.definitionFit: A base camp is the main station from which climbers or explorers set out.

clue.text: See 12
Ambitious person with leaflet on drugs?

parts.note: someone on drugs is high
a flyer is a printed leaflet

explanation.surface: A pamphlet promoting narcotics, handed out by a go-getter.
explanation.definitionFit: A high-flyer is someone with great ambition and potential for success.

clue.text: Work during curfew for Essex town member among reactionary readers

parts.note: Grays is a town in Essex, a county east of London

indicators.note: among says one piece sits inside another here
reactionary suggests going backwards, so the word for readers is turned round

parts.note: ye is an old word for you, the readers being addressed
a leg is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: A labourer works through the evening curfew to reach an Essex town, mixing with conservative newspaper readers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work' is the definition, not a verb: Gray's Elegy opens 'The curfew tolls the knell of parting day', so the poem is literally a work during curfew. 'reactionary' turns the readers' word backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Gray's famous poem begins as the evening curfew bell rings, so it is a literary work set at curfew.

clue.text: See 16
Sign page with former European monarch

parts.note: Leo is a sign of the zodiac
old means former, as in an old boss

explanation.surface: A page boy signs a document with a royal from the past.
explanation.definitionFit: Leopold was the name of kings of Belgium and Holy Roman emperors, European royalty.

clue.text: Fire starting on haystack engulfs busted dam of European monarch

indicators.note: starting signals that only the opening letter of fire is wanted
engulfs means one word swallows another inside it

parts.note: a rick is a stack of hay
the Eder dam was breached in the 1943 Dambusters raid

explanation.surface: A blaze that starts on a haystack spreads to a breached dam belonging to a king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'busted dam' alludes to the Dambusters, the RAF raid that broke the Möhne and Eder dams in Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: Several Prussian, Danish and other European kings bore this name, including Frederick the Great.

clue.text: Reduce amount of woodwind left in orchestra

indicators.note: amount of suggests a portion of the following words, the letters run across them

explanation.surface: Cut back the number of wind instruments left playing in the band.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwindle is to grow smaller; the verb here is used as shrink or diminish.

clue.text: Scene of 16 17 for Archy with cod and curry hunt

indicators.note: for here means the letters are exchanged for a new arrangement, the only anagram signal in the clue

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone called Archy goes hunting for cod and curry.
explanation.walkthrough: Araucaria gives almost no anagram signal here; 'for' is the only candidate. Gray's Elegy is set in a country churchyard, at Stoke Poges.
explanation.definitionFit: Gray's poem's full title is Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard, so that is where the poem takes place.

clue.text: One shrub to be trimmed before the fall?

indicators.note: trimmed suggests the shrub is cut and reshaped, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A bush needs pruning before autumn arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the fall' looks like autumn, but the proverb 'pride goes before a fall' is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: Hubris is overweening pride, which the proverb says comes before a fall.

clue.text: Cause bewilderment to prisoner unable to hide

parts.note: a con is a convict, a prisoner
someone found has failed to stay hidden

explanation.surface: An escaped convict is caught because there is nowhere left to hide.
explanation.definitionFit: To confound someone is to baffle or perplex them completely.

clue.text: Would-be 15, one taking vehicle to America

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a car is a vehicle
US is short for the United States, America

explanation.surface: Someone hoping to rise high takes a car over to America.
explanation.walkthrough: 15 is HIGH-FLYER; Icarus flew too near the sun on wax wings and fell, an aspiring high flyer.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Icarus tried to soar on wax wings and crashed, an aspiring flyer who flew too high.

clue.text: Prize for one being protected

parts.note: a means one, as in a single
a ward is someone under a guardian's protection

explanation.surface: An award given for someone kept safe.
explanation.definitionFit: An award is a prize given in recognition of merit.

clue.text: 11 sounds completely pulverised

indicators.note: sounds signals that the phrase is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: wholly ground means entirely crushed to powder

explanation.surface: A churchyard noise of something being totally crushed.
explanation.definitionFit: A churchyard is consecrated earth, land blessed for burial and so sacred.

clue.text: Bad guy in book hit off when there's a fiddler about

indicators.note: about means one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: Nero, the Roman emperor, is said to have fiddled while Rome burned; with a, A NERO

indicators.note: off suggests the word hit is knocked out of shape and rearranged

explanation.surface: A villain in a novel strikes out while someone plays the violin nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad guy' tempts you toward a villain, but the book's flawed protagonist is meant. Emperor Nero reputedly fiddled while Rome burned; 'off' scrambles the struck word into TIH.
explanation.definitionFit: An anti-hero is a central character in fiction lacking heroic virtues, so a flawed or bad protagonist.

clue.text: Tell us, with skill, where you live

definitions.meaning: to ... an audience is to speak to them
... as a noun means skill or dexterity, as in handling a task with ...

explanation.surface: A form asks you, politely, to give your home details.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers speaking to a gathering, deftness in doing something, and the location of one's home.

clue.text: Gilbertian Dick in block for rigging

definitions.meaning: Dick ... is the villainous sailor in Gilbert and Sullivan's HMS Pinafore
a flat wooden block with holes, used to tighten a ship's shrouds

explanation.definitionFit: The sailor's surname in the operetta is also the nautical term for a holed wooden block on a ship.
